doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Closing: saxophone writing and brass quintets
summary: Thanks, then his saxophone quartet piece and 'In a Pentatonic Mood'.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has been a fascinating conversation.
And I really appreciate you coming down here.
I know that your saxophone work too has gotten around, as we can see from this program in Japanese. Very interesting.
That was recorded, that “Modern Art Suite” by the New York Saxophone Quartet. Ray Beckenstein is sort of the leader of that group, a wonderful group of players.
Did your years in the big bands help you figure out what saxophones should and shouldn’t do or what you can write for them?

Yes, I think so, yes. Well having heard the instrument so many years by some of the great players, yes. I have some brass quintets that are published and one is in the process right now. I call it “In a Pentatonic Mood.” And if you ever notice, the pick-ups to “Sentimental Mood,” Duke’s, it’s a pentatonic scale. So those five notes are the same, and then it’s altogether different you know. But that’s the way I—
